message:
docs(release): the NAS handoff, and the route that does not exist

Written for whoever runs the NAS, by someone who did not touch it.

The finding that shapes it: the directory server has nine routes and none of
them serves an artifact. A manifest's artifact URLs point at files the server
will never hand out, so they have to be published on a static path
separately. That path is a condition of this release rather than a
suggestion, and changing it means rebuilding and re-signing the manifest --
the URLs are inside what was signed.

Also in it: the env delta, with REMOTE60_UPDATE_PUBLIC_KEY explained by what
it costs to omit (the server stops checking its own manifest before serving
it); the deployment order, artifacts verified in full before the manifest
goes last, because the reverse leaves a manifest pointing at files that are
not there yet; what a restart costs (host tokens survive, client sessions do
not); and the 409 behaviour for older clients, which is harmless as long as
the advertised observe port stays at http+1.

And a section for what the handoff does not establish -- the in-app update
running end to end, UI responsiveness, the auth header on the wire, the
downgrade refusal, and the current backend's version. The last one is not
"unknown": a TLS GET succeeded and the metadata was absent. What is unknown
is why.
